    - link "School lessons":

    - text: CLASS 12 · PROBABILITY
    - heading "Bayes' Theorem" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Updating prior source probabilities after observing evidence.
    - text: 40 min · INTERACTIVE · EXAMPLE-DRIVEN · LIVE CALC · proof · practice
    - navigation "Lesson sections":
      - button "Update"
      - button "Tree"
      - button "Formula"
      - button "Proof"
      - button "Practice"
      - button "Reset example":
        - img
    - heading "MACHINE QUALITY EXAMPLE (LIVE)" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Two machines produce items. Some are defective (D). Given an item is defective, what is the chance it came from Machine 2?
    - article:
      - heading "Source mix (priors)" [level=3]
      - text: P(M1)
      - slider "P(M1)": "0.6"
      - status: 60%
      - text: P(M2)
      - slider "P(M2)": "0.4"
      - status: 40%
    - article:
      - heading "Defect rates (likelihoods)" [level=3]
      - text: P(D | M1)
      - slider "P(D | M1)": "0.02"
      - status: 2%
      - text: P(D | M2)
      - slider "P(D | M2)": "0.05"
      - status: 5%
    - article:
      - heading "Live denominator" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(D)
      - status: 0.032 (3.2%)
    - article:
      - heading "Show posterior for" [level=3]
      - button "M2|D" [pressed]
      - button "M1|D"
    - article:
      - heading "1 PRIOR (Before evidence)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Imagine 100 items produced. Split by source (prior probabilities).
      - text: M1 (60 chips) 60% M2 (40 chips) 40%
      - strong: Total = 100 items
      - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "2 EVIDENCE D (Defective)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Expected defective items (total = 3.2). Keep only defective chips.
      - text: "From M1: 1.2 (60% × 2%) From M2: 2 (40% × 5%)"
      - strong: Total defective = 3.2
      - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "3 POSTERIOR (Given D)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Normalize the defect-only group. Updated probabilities given D.
      - img "Posterior M1 37.5%, M2 62.5%"
      - text: M1 | D = 37.5% M2 | D = 62.5%
      - strong: Sum = 100%
    - paragraph: Out of 3.2 expected defective items, 2 come from M2. Given D, the chance of M2 is 62.5%.
    - article:
      - heading "PROBABILITY TREE" [level=2]
      - text: Source (Prior) Defect Status (Likelihood) Joint (Path)
      - img "Two machine branches with defective and nondefective outcomes": M1 0.6 D (defective) 0.02 = 0.6 × 0.02 = 0.012 Not D 0.98 = 0.6 × 0.98 = 0.588 M2 0.4 D (defective) 0.05 = 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.02 Not D 0.95 = 0.4 × 0.95 = 0.38
      - paragraph: P(D) = 0.012 + 0.02 = 0.032
    - article:
      - heading "FORMULA BUILDER" [level=2]
      - heading "Bayes’ Theorem" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(M2 | D) = P(M2)P(D | M2) / P(D)
      - heading "Numerator (target path)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.02
      - heading "Denominator (all paths with D)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(D) = P(M₁)P(D | M₁) + P(M₂)P(D | M₂)
      - paragraph: = 0.6 × 0.02 + 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.032
      - heading "Quotient (posterior)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(M2 | D) = 0.02 / 0.032
      - strong: 0.625 = 62.5%
    - article:
      - heading "KEY TAKEAWAY" [level=2]
      - text: Don’t confuse these!
      - paragraph: P(D | M2) = 5%
      - paragraph: Chance of defect given the source is M2.
      - strong: vs
      - paragraph: P(M2 | D) = 62.5%
      - paragraph: Chance the source is M2 given the item is defective.
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Updated from 40% (prior) to 62.5% (posterior) after evidence D.
    - article:
      - heading "NATURAL FREQUENCY VIEW" [level=2]
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Stage M1 M2 Total":
            - columnheader "Stage"
            - columnheader "M1"
            - columnheader "M2"
            - columnheader "Total"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Prior (all items) 60 40 100":
            - rowheader "Prior (all items)"
            - cell "60"
            - cell "40"
            - cell "100"
          - row "Defect rate 2% 5% —":
            - rowheader "Defect rate"
            - cell "2%"
            - cell "5%"
            - cell "—"
          - row "Defective (expected) 1.2 2 3.2":
            - rowheader "Defective (expected)"
            - cell "1.2"
            - cell "2"
            - cell "3.2"
          - row "Posterior (given D) 37.5% 62.5% 100%":
            - rowheader "Posterior (given D)"
            - cell "37.5%"
            - cell "62.5%"
            - cell "100%"
      - paragraph: Filter by evidence, then renormalize.
    - article:
      - heading "REASONING STEPS" [level=2]
      - list:
        - listitem: Start with prior probabilities of each source.
        - listitem: Multiply each prior by its likelihood of evidence to get its joint contribution.
        - listitem: Sum the contributions to get P(D).
        - listitem: Divide each contribution by P(D) to get posterior probabilities, provided P(D) > 0.
      - paragraph: P(Mᵢ | D) = P(Mᵢ ∩ D)/P(D), which gives Bayes’ formula.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - text: Mixing up directions.
      - paragraph: "P(D | M2): defect rate if from M2 (known forward quality data)."
      - paragraph: "P(M2 | D): updated belief about source after seeing a defect."
      - paragraph: They answer different questions. Their values can coincide, but the conditionals are not interchangeable.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE (MACHINE QUALITY)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Given: P(M₁) = 0.60, P(M₂) = 0.40, P(D | M₁) = 0.02, P(D | M₂) = 0.05."
      - heading "1. Total defect probability" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(D) = 0.60 × 0.02 + 0.40 × 0.05 = 0.032
      - heading "2. Posterior for M2 given D" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(M₂ | D) = 0.020 / 0.032 = 0.625 = 62.5%
      - paragraph: Given an item is defective, the probability it came from Machine 2 is 62.5%.
    - article:
      - heading "TRY IT YOURSELF" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "A factory uses two suppliers: P(S1) = 70%; P(S2) = 30% P(D | S1) = 1%; P(D | S2) = 4%"
      - text: Given an item is defective, what is P(S2 | D)?
      - group "Choose the posterior":
        - text: Choose the posterior
        - radio "40.0%"
        - text: 40.0%
        - radio "46.2%"
        - text: 46.2%
        - radio "54.3%"
        - text: 54.3%
        - radio "63.2%"
        - text: 63.2%
      - button "Check Answer"
      - button "Show solution"
